habitat: Singly or in pairs in lightly wooded country and suburbia. It perches on a branch, post or wire and flies to the ground for insects and other small prey.
summary: A very common resident in Newman's account: heavy-bodied, heavy-billed and long-tailed, completely pied, with a white wing-bar that reaches the shoulder. The female has rufous flanks, often hard to see. The immature is ash-brown above and greyish brown below, finely barred. The call is a harsh gercha, gercha or skiza, skiza, and there is also a rambling song. The western race has a variable white eyebrow; that race is not treated as the Kruger bird. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Fiscal Flycatcher has a thinner bill, and its wing-bar does not reach the shoulder.
A female Red-backed Shrike has more rufous upperparts than an immature Southern Fiscal and lacks white wing-bars.

calls.description: A harsh gercha, gercha or skiza, skiza. There is also a rambling song with sweet notes and the gercha sound. Grade A call from near Barkly East in the Eastern Cape. The filename is XC309835-Common fiscal exc.mp3, so the file is marked as an excerpt.

research.note: Newman calls it a very common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged, as were the population figures. The western race L. c. subcoronatus has a variable white eyebrow and is not stored as the Kruger plumage. Pied is not split into separate black and white tokens where Newman does not itemise the parts.
